content.title: Review the default market overview instrument set and row fields
content.intent: Prove the market overview shows the four required instruments and that each row exposes value, daily percentage, and sparkline.
content.technique_notes: Applied equivalence partitioning to the required instrument set and per-row field presence because this path validates the baseline representative state of the overview. Negative, boundary, auth, and pagination techniques were not applicable because the source describes a read-only dashboard module with no user-entered inputs, access rule, or result-set variation. Budget estimate remained 4 scenarios, under the ceiling of 8, so no cut was needed.

content.title: Hover a market row without changing layout
content.intent: Prove the hover treatment does not change the hovered row height or move neighboring content.
content.technique_notes: Applied state/flow reasoning to compare the pre-hover and hover states of the same row, focused on visual stability promises that often regress during UI styling changes. Negative and boundary techniques were not applicable because the source defines one hover behavior, not an input range or failure path. Budget estimate remained 4 scenarios, under the ceiling of 8, so no cut was needed.

content.title: Hover a market row to reveal emphasis and sparkline enlargement
content.intent: Prove hovering a market row changes it to the emphasized hover state and enlarges that row's sparkline region.
content.technique_notes: Applied state/flow reasoning because hover is a state transition from the default row presentation to the hover presentation. I kept emphasis and sparkline enlargement together because the source states them as the positive hover outcome, while layout stability was separated as a distinct edge path. Budget estimate remained 4 scenarios, under the ceiling of 8, so no cut was needed.

content.title: Refresh the same market overview state and confirm deterministic sparklines
content.intent: Prove the market overview re-renders the same sparkline traces for the same state because the sparklines use deterministic mock data.
content.technique_notes: Applied persistence/refresh-style reasoning to repeated rendering of the same overview state so the path proves sameness across renders, not just presence on one render. Boundary, negative, auth, and concurrency techniques were not applicable because the source defines a display determinism promise without input ranges, write operations, or access branches. Budget estimate remained 4 scenarios, under the ceiling of 8, so no cut was needed.

judgements.rationale: [applicability] I judged equivalence partitioning applicable because the use-case promises a fixed representative set of four instruments and a fixed representative set of per-row fields. I judged state/flow applicable because hover changes the row from a default visual state to a hover visual state.

[applicability] I judged persistence applicable in a limited way for repeated rendering because deterministic mock-data implies the same view state should reproduce the same sparkline traces after a refresh or re-render.

[applicability] I judged boundary value analysis, negative/error, auth, CRUD, idempotency, concurrency, pagination, i18n, notification, and file/media not applicable because the source names no constrained input, failure semantics, permissions, persisted mutation, collection controls, localization behavior, asynchronous side effect, or upload surface for this use-case.
[value_score] Highest value because it proves the baseline instrument coverage and row anatomy that the investment professional depends on before any interaction.
[value_score] High value because layout-shift regressions are subtle but directly undermine side-by-side scanning even when content still appears correct.
[value_score] Moderate-high value because the positive hover feedback is part of the promised inspection affordance, but its absence is usually more visible than layout drift.
[value_score] Moderate value because deterministic mock data matters for consistent interpretation and stable tests, though it is less central than baseline visibility and hover stability.
